briefing: Compute procurement is the story of the day: CNBC reports Anthropic and OpenAI are now chasing 20-30 MW data center deals across the US, UK and Nordics alongside their gigawatt megaprojects, prioritizing speed to usable capacity as large builds slip. Nvidia's Jensen Huang added fuel, saying at a UK AI safety summit hosted by King Charles III that the company expects to sell twice as many chips next year. On safety and governance, Anthropic announced a $1B+ each, five-year 'embedded evaluation' partnership with Accenture's Faculty unit, putting outside evaluators inside the company with employee-level access - the first concrete implementation of Dario Amodei's 'pace the frontier' thesis. Brussels moved in the opposite direction on consumer AI: the EU KIDS Act would force AI companions off by default for all minors, ban under-13s outright, and shift the burden of proof to platforms, with fines up to 6% of global turnover. Security remains the soft underbelly - Hacktron AI used Claude and GPT-5.6 Sol to compromise OpenAI employee ChatGPT accounts in an authorized test, compressing months of offensive work into days.

items.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI hunt for smaller 20-30 MW data center deals
items.summary: Both labs are negotiating much smaller compute allocations alongside their gigawatt-scale commitments, with Anthropic sounding out deals across the UK and the Nordics and both exploring similar US deployments, sources told CNBC.
items.why_it_matters: Signals that speed to usable capacity now rivals scale as a constraint, as megaprojects face delays, local opposition and power shortages.

items.headline: Anthropic and Accenture commit $1B+ each to 'embedded evaluation' of frontier AI
items.summary: Anthropic announced a five-year partnership with Accenture's Faculty AI unit in which external evaluators get internal, employee-level access to observe model training, review deployment decisions and report incidents.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first concrete operationalization of third-party oversight inside a frontier lab, a template regulators and rivals will be measured against.

items.headline: EU KIDS Act would switch AI companions off by default for all minors
items.summary: The European Commission's proposal bans under-13s from companion chatbots entirely, turns companion features off by default for everyone under 18, bars cross-session memory and emotional-dependency designs, and carries fines up to 6% of global turnover.
items.why_it_matters: It targets the core retention mechanics of Character.AI, Replika and chatbot features on social platforms, and shifts the burden of proof onto providers before launch.

items.headline: Jensen Huang: Nvidia will sell twice as many chips next year
items.summary: Speaking at an AI summit hosted by King Charles III in Scotland, the Nvidia CEO said chip unit sales will double next year, following guidance of roughly 70% revenue growth for the fiscal year ending January 2028.
items.why_it_matters: A blunt rebuttal to AI slowdown narratives from the company whose order book is the industry's demand thermometer.

items.headline: Hacktron AI used Claude and GPT-5.6 Sol to breach OpenAI employee accounts
items.summary: In an authorized bug-bounty investigation, researchers chained an exploit through an OpenAI staff Discourse forum to reach employee ChatGPT accounts and open a harmless pull request against OpenAI code on GitHub; OpenAI says the flaws are fixed.
items.why_it_matters: Frontier models are now simultaneously targets, defensive tools and offensive research assistants, collapsing attack timelines from months to days.

items.headline: Anthropic says Claude sped up 30+ open-source biomolecular models
items.summary: New Anthropic research reports Claude optimized more than 30 open-source biomolecular models in about four weeks for roughly 4x speedups, with a low-memory mode enabling >10,000-token structure prediction on a single Nvidia GPU node; all code is being open-sourced.
items.why_it_matters: A concrete AI-for-science result that lowers the compute floor for protein design, paired with a $1M Claude-credit design competition with Adaptyv Bio.

items.headline: Crusoe raises $3.9B at a $30.9B valuation and pivots toward smaller sites
items.summary: The neocloud behind OpenAI's Texas complex closed an initial Series F tranche with Nvidia, Founders Fund, Mubadala, GIC, QIA and TPG participating, and told the WSJ it is now investing in faster, cheaper small-scale data centers.
items.why_it_matters: Compute scarcity is attracting infrastructure-style capital, and even the largest builders are hedging toward distributed capacity.

items.headline: Cohere and Aleph Alpha to merge into a transatlantic enterprise-AI challenger
items.summary: The Canadian and German model makers plan dual headquarters in Toronto and Berlin with more than 1,000 employees, targeting a close later this year subject to regulatory approval.
items.why_it_matters: Consolidation among non-US frontier-adjacent labs, aimed at sovereign and regulated enterprise buyers wary of US cloud exposure.

items.headline: OpenAI expands ChatGPT ads with 'Sponsored Agents'
items.summary: New advertising tools let a business open a labeled, separate chat with a user after an ad click, alongside natural-language campaign creation and analytics.
items.why_it_matters: Moves ChatGPT monetization from placement to conversation, raising fresh disclosure and conflict-of-interest questions for assistant recommendations.

items.headline: Mistral brings private AI into Firefox's Smart Window
items.summary: Mistral and Mozilla launched private, multilingual AI in Firefox's Smart Window for France and North America, with the UK and Germany planned later in 2026.
items.why_it_matters: A privacy-positioned distribution channel for a European model provider inside a mainstream browser.

items.headline: Hardcoded secrets found in 12% of credential slots in public MCP configs
items.summary: Hush Security analyzed roughly 82,000 public Model Context Protocol configuration files and found hardcoded secrets exposing AI coding tool credentials in about 12% of credential slots.
items.why_it_matters: Agent tooling is inheriting classic secrets-management failures at scale, right as agents gain write access to production systems.

items.headline: India Deep Tech Alliance members put ~Rs 2,170 crore into 56 deep-tech startups
items.summary: In its first year, alliance members including Accel, Blume, 3one4, Celesta and Chiratae invested roughly Rs 639 crore into 16 AI companies and Rs 649 crore across quantum, robotics and space.
items.why_it_matters: A rare data point on how non-US private capital is allocating across the AI stack rather than into frontier models.
